page.layout: One column of running text, with the chapter heading "IN CAP. XVIII." in the middle of the page. Margin marks: a small "I" in the left margin beside "Art.1.". No text in the right margin. Catchword "per" at the lower right.

main_text.p: siue natio seruorum eius, id est, pij administri eius calceati praeparatione Euangelij pacis, non est delicias actura in terra aut electro, sed vitam asperam seuerámque victura in pellibus & coactili o-pere ad iter faciendum & iniuriam depellendam commodo. Nam propterea subiicit Poeta: Questi la caccierà per ogni villa, &c. his fugabit eam lupam per omnem vicum, Donec ipsam remiserit in infernum. Eò unde inuidia primùm ipsam dididerat. Hæc germana Dantis, pij & sapientis & grauis Poetæ, sententia. Quamobrem in sequentibus omnibus disputator οὐδὲν πρὸς ὥρας [?]. Coniungantur his quæ dicit Ioannes Apoc.13.& 18. de nundinatione & auaritia Ecclesiam occupatura, & in orbem inundatura ex meretricis gremio: plana hæc omnia futura sunt.
main_text.head: IN CAP. XVIII.
main_text.p: IArt.1. venias peccatorum auditoribus pollicentur, cum Pontificis testimonium nullum proferre possint. hoc ita nec Landinus dixit. nec Dantes angustè sensit. Hic enim Poeta grauissimus in Cantico 29. pio & arguto illo, postquam de vanitate & indignitate cucullatorum dixisset, his verbis vtitur: Sed ea auis in ore cucullæ siue capitij nidulatur, Quam si vulgus vidisset, visura esset Indulgentiam, de qua confidit sibi. Qua tanta illusio in terra creuit, Vt sine probatione vllius testimonij ad omnem promissionem concurrent. Hac re pinguefacit porcum sanctus Antonius, Et a'y præterea, qui adhuc magis sunt porci. Soluendo moneta sine charactere. Non dicit Dantes de testimonio bullato Pontificis, sed de testimonio diuino per

page.notes: Greek phrase after "disputator" is hard to read; the letters are uncertain, so it is marked [?]. "Quesli" in the italic Italian quotation is read as "Questi" (the long s and t are unclear). "dididerat" is printed as it appears in the scan. The word "a'y" in the Latin quotation is likely a printing or reading error for "ay", and is left as read. The catchword "per" is at the lower right, below the last line; it is not repeated in the text. The "I" in the left margin is a section mark, shown as a note. The text continues on the next page after "per".
